chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahzar, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hurayz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah ibn A'yun, who said: I asked Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him):

Is the Takbir on the days of Tashriq said after the prayers? He replied: The Takbir is in Mina after fifteen prayers, and in the provinces after ten prayers. The first Takbir is after the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice, saying: 'God is the Greatest, God is the Greatest, there is no god but God, and God is the Greatest, God is the Greatest, and to God belongs the praise, God is the Greatest for what He guided us to, and God is the Greatest for what He provided us with from the grazing livestock.' And the Takbir was established in the other provinces after ten prayers, such that when the people depart in the first departure, the people of the provinces refrain from the Takbir, and the people of Mina continue to say it as long as they are in Mina until the final departure.

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: The days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhul-Hijja) following Eid al-Adha

ai.seo_question: What are the specific rules and timings for reciting Takbir during the days of Tashriq in Mina versus other provinces?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal details the distinct jurisprudential rulings for the Takbir al-Tashriq, differentiating between the continuous recitation in Mina after fifteen prayers and the restricted recitation in other provinces after ten prayers. It highlights the scholarly emphasis on the temporal and spatial boundaries of ritual commemoration, linking the proclamation of God's greatness to the specific events of Eid al-Adha and the departure from Arafat. This distinction underscores the Shia tradition's adherence to the Prophet's practice as transmitted through the Imams, ensuring the ritual's integrity across different geographical contexts.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 15-4 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Ali ibn Mahzyar, on the authority of Hammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Hurayz ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Zurarah ibn A’ayn, “I asked Abi Ja’far As-Sadiq, ‘Are the Takbirs on the days of Tashriq to be said after fifteen units of prayers?’

The Imam (MGB) replied, ‘You must say the Takbirs after fifteen units of prayers in Mina and after ten units of prayers elsewhere. On the day of the offering and after the noon prayer you must say, ‘Allahu akbarullahu akbarullahu akbar, La ilaha illallah Allahu akbar Allahu akbar va lillahi-hamd Allahu akbar Ala mahadana Vallahu Akbar Ala Ma Razaqna Men Bahimat al-An’am.’ This is to be said after ten units of prayers elsewhere since the people start to move from Mina (on the 12th day of Dhul-Hijja) and those who are at Mina should say these Takbirs until the last person.”
